implementation.name: Erlang/OTP BEAM runtime
implementation.version_scope: Erlang/OTP compilation and module loading; the retrieved system documentation is OTP 29.1.1.

sources.label: Erlang systems, concurrency and OTP libraries
Erlang shell, modules, exports and pattern matching
Erlang/OTP compilation, BEAM and code replacement

fit.text: Build concurrent, distributed systems; OTP adds libraries and design principles for application structure.

prerequisites.text: Install Erlang/OTP and learn modules, function arities and pattern matching; the introductory guide assumes programming basics.

execution.text: The compiler produces BEAM object code; the runtime code server loads modules for execution.

behavior.text: Module names match .erl filenames, exports identify callable function/arities, and pattern matching directs function clauses.

tooling.text: The erl shell supports interactive evaluation and c(Module) compilation; erlc compiles files from the OS shell.

maintenance.text: Code replacement keeps current and old module variants; a further replacement can terminate processes still running the purged version.

costs.text: Erlang/OTP uses Apache-2.0 terms for covered components; bundled third-party and application libraries keep separate notices.

example.run_instructions: From the directory containing reader.erl, start erl. At its prompt enter c(reader). and then reader:total(). including the final full stops.
example.expected_result: Compilation reports {ok,reader}; the function call evaluates to 12.

licenses.scope: Erlang/OTP covered source/runtime components; separately marked third-party material is excluded.
licenses.notice: Retain the implementation license and relevant notices when redistributing it.

sources.label: F# project creation and .NET CLI workflow

fit.text: F# builds .NET programs with functional programming and interoperability with other .NET languages and libraries.

prerequisites.text: Install the .NET SDK and learn expressions, immutable bindings, functions and pattern matching.

execution.text: The .NET CLI builds F# projects and runs a console application's entry point.

behavior.text: Type inference and immutable defaults shape ordinary code; .NET types and libraries remain available.

tooling.text: The CLI supports multi-project solutions and references; editor support complements the same SDK toolchain.

maintenance.text: Keep SDK, target framework and package versions with the project so compilation and runtime requirements are identifiable.

costs.text: The F# compiler's covered source uses MIT; the .NET distribution and imported packages have independent component notices.

example.run_instructions: Create a console project using dotnet new console -lang F# -o PLLDNExample, replace its Program.fs with this code, then run dotnet run --project PLLDNExample.

implementation.name: FStar proof-oriented programming system
implementation.version_scope: FStar language tutorial and implementation documentation checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: F* combines a dependently typed language with proof assistance for programs whose properties are expressed alongside their implementation.

prerequisites.text: Learn functions, refinement types and proof obligations; a module name must match its .fst filename.

execution.text: The default tool checks source without executing it; extraction to a target language is a separate workflow.

behavior.text: A refinement narrows a type to values satisfying a predicate; checked properties remain scoped to the stated definitions and assumptions.

tooling.text: Emacs and VS Code plugins support incremental checking, navigation and editing.

maintenance.text: Keep the checker and supporting toolchain identified; verification and extracted-program execution are distinct evidence.

costs.text: The FStar implementation uses Apache-2.0; extraction targets, solvers and libraries have separate component terms.

example.code:
module Addition

let total : x:int { x = 5 } = 2 + 3
example.run_instructions: Save Addition.fst and check it with the installed F* compiler through a configured Emacs or VS Code F* plugin, as described in the tutorial.
example.expected_result: The checker should accept the refinement that total equals 5. This checking workflow does not run an application or emit console output.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The compiler/system source grant is separate from licenses of extracted target libraries and proof dependencies.

implementation.name: Factor language implementation
implementation.version_scope: Factor guided tour and first-program documentation checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: Factor supplies a compiled, dynamically typed concatenative language with libraries for application code and domain-specific languages.

prerequisites.text: Learn the data stack, words and vocabulary imports; the guided tour assumes some previous programming experience.

execution.text: Code can be evaluated interactively in the listener or compiled and deployed as an application.

behavior.text: Words compose by consuming and producing stack values; dynamic types and garbage collection belong to the selected implementation.

tooling.text: The listener, vocabulary-based development, help browser and testing workflow are documented in the first-program tutorial.

maintenance.text: Use documentation matching the selected image and library vocabularies; file paths can differ across platforms.

costs.text: The selected implementation uses BSD-2-Clause; separately linked native libraries retain their own notices.

example.run_instructions: Start the installed Factor language environment and evaluate this snippet in its listener. The same source can be saved as hello.factor for a configured Factor project.
example.expected_result: Prints PLLDN in the Factor listener.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.

implementation.name: Fantom launcher, compiler and pod system
implementation.version_scope: Fantom introductory documentation, revision 1.0.83, checked on 2026-10-13; selected workflow uses the JVM.

fit.text: Fantom supplies JVM scripting, reusable pod modules and web-application libraries in one language environment.

prerequisites.text: The introductory JVM workflow requires Java 8 or later and the Fantom bin directory on PATH; learn classes and methods.

execution.text: fan runs a .fan script containing a class and main method; precompiled applications can be launched from pods.

behavior.text: Arguments need not be parameters of main because the environment also exposes them through Env.args.

tooling.text: fansh provides interactive evaluation and the build toolkit constructs versioned pod modules.

maintenance.text: Identify the Fantom distribution, pods and Java host together; a published tutorial's sample launcher version is not a latest-release claim.

costs.text: Fantom's covered distribution uses AFL-3.0; the JVM and added libraries have separate terms.

example.run_instructions: With Fantom and its configured Java host installed, run fan hello.fan.

implementation.name: Faust DSP compiler
implementation.version_scope: Faust quick-start/compiler documentation and distribution grant checked on 2026-10-13.

sources.label: Faust code generation and architecture files

fit.text: Faust describes audio signal processing and generates code to embed in an audio application or selected architecture.

prerequisites.text: Learn signal inputs, outputs and composition; a generated DSP class needs a host to provide and consume audio buffers.

execution.text: The command-line compiler emits C++ by default and supports other targets; architecture files can wrap the generated processing code.

behavior.text: The process definition determines signal connections; multiplying a signal by a constant scales its samples.

tooling.text: Faust offers compiler options, architecture wrappers and an online editing workflow for DSP experiments.

maintenance.text: Keep target backend, compiler and chosen architecture identified; sample rate and host routing affect observed audio behavior.

costs.text: The compiler grant is LGPL-2.1-or-later; architecture files, DSP libraries and application hosts require separate review.

example.run_instructions: Generate the DSP class with faust gain.dsp -o gain.cpp. Use a suitable Faust architecture or audio host to supply one input channel and read one output channel.
example.expected_result: Compilation produces a DSP class; when hosted, an input sample 0.8 produces 0.4. The source itself does not open an audio device.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The checked compiler grant states LGPL version 2.1 or later. This expression does not assign the compiler's terms to every generated audio application.

prerequisites.text: Install the selected Fennel executable with a supported Lua or LuaJIT host; learn Lisp forms and Lua's value model.

execution.text: The executable evaluates Fennel or compiles it to Lua; shipping compiled Lua need not include the compiler.

behavior.text: Functions and lexical values follow the documented Lua-like semantics, with differences called out in the tutorial.

tooling.text: The project provides a REPL, reference, macro guide and embedding API.

maintenance.text: Record the Fennel compiler and Lua host together; packaged compiler versions can lag behind official releases.

costs.text: Fennel uses MIT; Lua, LuaJIT and imported application libraries have separate licenses.

example.run_instructions: With the installed Fennel executable and its Lua host available, run fennel hello.fnl, using the executable's versioned name if required.

implementation.name: GNU Gforth interpreter and image
implementation.version_scope: Current Gforth manual and source grants checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: Forth organizes computations as words operating on a data stack; this profile selects Gforth's interpreter and image environment.

prerequisites.text: Learn postfix arithmetic and stack effects before composing words; install a matching Gforth engine and image.

execution.text: gforth reads source files or enters an interactive session; -e supplies additional Forth code.

behavior.text: Arithmetic consumes the top stack values; word order determines evaluation without infix parentheses.

tooling.text: The manual documents command history, source loading, image options and different diagnostic engine variants.

maintenance.text: Keep the engine, image and source libraries matched; loaded state can affect an interactive session's results.

costs.text: Gforth's checked engine grant is GPL-3.0-or-later; other Forth systems and foreign libraries have different terms.

example.run_instructions: Run gforth total.fs -e bye. The -e bye argument exits after loading the source file.
example.expected_result: Prints 5, with the Forth output word's normal spacing.

licenses.scope: The named implementation only; dependencies and host runtimes have separate terms.
licenses.notice: The current Gforth engine grant states GPL version 3 or later; this does not characterize every historical release or Forth implementation.

implementation.name: GNU Fortran (gfortran) from GCC 15.2.0
implementation.version_scope: GCC 15.2.0 compiler sources and invocation manual; intrinsic documentation checked on 2026-10-13.

fit.text: Array arithmetic and numerical procedures are concrete uses of this compiled Fortran implementation; SUM reduces an array to a scalar.

prerequisites.text: Install gfortran and its matching runtime. Distinguish free-form .f90 input from fixed-form legacy source.

execution.text: gfortran compiles and links source into an executable; libgfortran provides language runtime services.

behavior.text: Declarations determine element types; array intrinsics express operations across multiple values. Bounds checks are available through compiler options.

tooling.text: The CLI provides dialect selection, warnings and -fcheck runtime diagnostics, including bounds checks.

maintenance.text: Choose source-format and dialect flags deliberately. Foreign-language interfaces must agree on calling conventions as well as symbol names.

costs.text: The compiler is GPL-3.0-or-later; libgfortran adds the GCC Runtime Library Exception. Its conditions matter when distributing linked programs.

example.code:
program total
  implicit none
  integer :: values(2) = (/ 2, 3 /)
  print *, sum(values)
end program total
example.run_instructions: Run gfortran total.f90 -o total, then run the produced executable: ./total on a Unix shell or .\total.exe on Windows.
example.expected_result: Prints the integer 5; list-directed output may include leading spaces.
